source_title: OpenClaw AMA — Deep Dive with Creator Peter Steinberger (AI Engineer Europe 2026)
speakers: Peter Steinberger (Creator of OpenClaw, now at OpenAI)
Shawn Wang / Swyx (AI Engineer conference founder)
key_insight: Iterative with taste as the bottleneck beats dark factory; concurrency is a workaround until tokens are faster (10 to 5-6 sessions trajectory); European harness sovereignty comes from plugin governance + risk tolerance a US big lab legally can't match; soul.md is load-bearing because consumer channels expect personality.
talking_points: Closed Claw concerns — Peter at OpenAI + broad sponsorship to avoid takeover appearance
Local and open models importance — European at heart, clanker bypasses enterprise silos
Peter's coding workflow — prompt request not pull request, 10 peak to 5-6 now
Dark Factory vs Iterative — first idea never the final project, taste is the bottleneck
Taste definition — lowest level 'doesn't stink like AI', higher level delightful details like OpenClaw roasts
Soul.md as key innovation — WhatsApp needed personality Claude Code didn't have
OpenClaw could only come from someone like Peter — big US labs legally can't ship it
Dream stack — ubiquitous agents, Star Trek computer, canvas on every screen, work.openclaw + home.openclaw federation
Prompt injection — frontier models detect it, untrusted content tagging, small local models are dangerous, Simon Willison dual-LLM is smart
Future skills — taste, system design, saying NO, big picture thinking
Dreaming feature — memory reconciliation like sleep garbage collection, Anthropic also building it per source leak
Plugin architecture — everything is a plugin, like Linux, don't need PRs for experiments
key_quotes: Everyone in the industry wins if more people spend time with AI
European at heart. You want to own your data
Much cooler automation use cases that large companies can never do
At some point this is not natural that you work on 6 things at the same time. It's a workaround until tokens are faster
I don't think you can build good software by specifying everything up front
The way to the mountain is usually never a straight line
First idea about a project is very unlikely to be the final project
Madness with a touch of science fiction
Saying no is becoming more and more important
If you don't think about boundaries you swipe yourself into a corner
Even the wildest idea is a prompt away. But this + this + this + this fitting together is the problem
I still remember Simon Willison saying he's been doing it 2 years and still figuring out what works
Understanding the theory will not make you better at using the tools
Like Linux — you install your own parts

Independent confirmation of OpenClaw memory innovations
Three-layer memory reconciliation = Peter's dreaming feature (independent convergence)
SOUL.md/USER.md/MEMORY.md layering derives from Peter's soul.md pattern
Peter cites Simon Willison's dual-LLM approach and '2 years still figuring out' quote
German satirical tutorial that validates Peter's 'unlimited access is the hard problem' point
Direct pair — same speaker, same conference, same day. State of Claw = product/architecture update; this AMA = philosophy/operator worldview. Read as one unit.
